newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Released Malaysian diplomat returning from Peru.
newsitem.headline: Released Malaysian diplomat returning from Peru.

text.p: Malaysia's ambassador to Peru, Ahmad Mokhtar Selat, who was released on Sunday after 12 days of captivity by Peruvian rebels, will arrive here on Wednesday, the national Bernama news agency reported on Monday.
He will be accompanied by his family and Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi, who flew to Lima last week on a "special mission" to seek an early release of Ahmad Mokhtar.
The foreign minister's arrival in Peru sparked speculation that Kuala Lumpur was trying to cut a private deal with the rebels, which Badawi has denied.

Ahmad Mokhtar was among a group of 20 hostages freed on Sunday by the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement guerrillas who seized the Japanese ambassador's residence and took captive hundreds of people attending a reception on December 17.
Badawi had left Lima for Mexico on Saturday. When the announcement of Ahmad Mokhtar's release came five hours later, the minister took the next plane back to the Peruvian capital, Bernama reported.
